summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console focusing on per-route usage lenses, cost breakdown, and how to map Harborline routes to chargeback buckets. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, security needs (KMS/SSO), and next steps for a pilot and perf baseline.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-01 16:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Maya, Carlos (Redwood) — Leila, Samir, Jordan (Harborline)

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. carlos is our solutions engineer. quick sound check?
[00:10] Leila Wong: sounds good, can you hear me? yes, good.
[00:12] Carlos Rivera: yep loud and clear. all right i'll drive the console tour and maya will jump in on business/contract stuff.
[00:18] Samir Desai: great, we really want to understand how to map our endpoints to costs, we have a bunch of microroutes and it's messy now.
[00:26] Maya Patel: perfect that's the goal — show how per-route lenses work and how you can tie that into your finance chargeback.
[00:32] [SCREEN SHARE START] Carlos Rivera: ok i'm in the console, top nav, select "Usage" -> "Lenses". first view is overall token throughput and cost burn by day. note the default view aggregates by model and route but you can pivot.
[00:50] Jordan Pike: quick q — can we get this to show our internal route names? we use svc-user-auth vs user-auth-prod etc.
[00:58] Carlos Rivera: yep that's the route tag mapping feature. you can provide a naming regex or an explicit map. i'll show a mapping rule in a sec.
[01:05] [00:60] Maya Patel: small note, when customers send their route list we usually recommend cleaning them to canonical names first — reduces noisy splits when you do chargeback.
[01:15] Leila Wong: ok, show us the cost breakdown for a route.
[01:20] Carlos Rivera: switching to per-route detail — pick route "auth/login" in this demo org. top is tokens and latency histogram, below is cost breakdown: infrastructure cost, model cost, and caching savings.
[01:35] Carlos Rivera: you'll see a column for "cache hit" percentage — our prefix and KV cache can shave off tokens significantly on sessionized traffic.
[01:45] Samir Desai: how accurate is the infra vs model split? finance will want to see exact numbers for chargebacks.
[01:50] Carlos Rivera: we attribute infra proportional to GPU time and model cost proportional to token compute using our runtime telemetry. it's an estimate but we expose the formula and raw counters so you can audit. sometimes transcription note: "atribute" spoken as "a-tribute" by SE.
[02:10] [02:15] Jordan Pike: any way to bucket by SLA tier? like customer-facing routes vs internal?
[02:20] Carlos Rivera: yes, apply tags or route groups and the dashboard can slice by those groups. we also have saved views for billing teams.
[02:30] Maya Patel: important part — we'll show the route-to-billing mapping panel. you can drag routes into buckets (product A, product B, infra overhead), or import a CSV map.
[02:45] [03:00] Samir Desai: our main concern is latency SLOs when batching — we can't sacrifice p95. how does batching interact with per-route cost?
[03:10] Carlos Rivera: good question. batching reduces cost per token but increases p50/p95 depending on arrival pattern. in the consoles "Optimize" hints we simulate batching impact using your real arrival distribution and show expected latency delta vs cost savings. here try the estimator.
[03:30] [03:35] Carlos Rivera: (click) estimator shows for route auth/login with your sample qps we could batch to 16 and save ~22% cost with p95 increase from 120ms to 180ms.
[03:48] Leila Wong: 180ms p95 is borderline for us. we run some auth flows in user-critical path. can we set per-route latency caps?
[03:56] Carlos Rivera: absolutely — routing policies allow per-route latency SLOs, which picks lower-batch windows and can route to a lower-latency model variant or dedicated backbone if enabled.
[04:10] [04:20] Samir Desai: this is helpful. about dedicated vs hosted — what triggers moving a route to Dedicated? is it pure qps or cost predictability?
[04:30] Maya Patel: two big levers: predictable throughput and data isolation. many customers start hosted to move fast, then move heavy traffic routes or regulated data to Dedicated. pricing is different — we can show a modeled cost comparison based on your QPS.
[04:42] Carlos Rivera: also note you can pin a route to a model variant with quantized weights; that often reduces infra slices without full Dedicated.
[04:50] [05:00] Jordan Pike: security — we need KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML integration, and regional data residency. do you support all those?
[05:08] Maya Patel: yes — Private + Dedicated options for residency and VPC, integrations with customer KMS, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. i'll attach the security pack after the call.
[05:18] Leila Wong: are the audit logs immutable? finance needs tamper-evidence for billing disputes.
[05:24] Carlos Rivera: yes they are append-only and can be exported to your logging bucket with retention controls.
[05:30] [05:45] Carlos Rivera: back to the console — here's a small anomaly detector for cost spikes. it alerts on route-level burn rate vs baseline and sends to Slack or webhook.
[05:55] Samir Desai: can that feed into autoscaling policies? we want automatic fallback to a cheaper model if cost spikes.
[06:02] Carlos Rivera: yep that's part of our routing policies — cost-based fallback will route to a cheaper model variant or lower precision quantized model automatically.
[06:15] [06:30] Leila Wong: are you able to show a real customer mapping quickly?
[06:33] Carlos Rivera: i pulled a sanitized example — look at these three buckets: "public-api", "internal-ml", "batch-ingest". public-api has highest p95 and token churn, internal-ml has big embeddings churn. you can toggle and see how cost concentrates.
[06:48] Maya Patel: note that for billing we usually recommend a hybrid: charge product teams by route consumer and keep an org-level infra overhead bucket.
[06:55] [07:10] Jordan Pike: ok how do we get the 3 canonical routes to you — CSV? api?
[07:15] Carlos Rivera: either is fine. CSV with columns route_name, tag, owner, cost_center works best for an initial import.
[07:22] Samir Desai: i want to validate the math — can you send the raw counters we can reconcile with our telemetry?
[07:28] Carlos Rivera: yes we expose raw counters and the attribution formula in the UI and via API. we'll include the export script.
[07:35] [08:00] Leila Wong: on the perf side we have an internal GPU fleet and also run spot instances; are there any gotchas with quantized models on older GPUs?
[08:12] Carlos Rivera: older GPUs sometimes miss optimized kernels for int8 paths, which can reduce throughput gains. we include compatibility notes in the model catalog and our Optimize tool proposes model variants suited to your hardware.
[08:25] Maya Patel: for a pilot we'll propose a small baseline run with representative traffic to measure p95 and tokens per call. carlos will recommend quantization and batching profiles and we can compare hosted vs dedicated cost projections.
[08:38] [09:00] Samir Desai: what about SLO-based expo pricing? can we lock a p95 SLA for a particular route?
[09:10] Maya Patel: SLA for Dedicated support includes latency targets for pinned models. Hosted SLA is at the account level; for route-level p95 guarantees we typically use Dedicated or a private deployment.
[09:22] [09:40] Carlos Rivera: switching to the "Chargeback" tab — here's how we map routes to billing codes; you can create rules and preview invoice lines. the preview is what finance sees if you export into your billing system.
[09:58] Jordan Pike: nice, can we transform names in the UI? we have internal prefixes to strip.
[10:05] Carlos Rivera: yes include a rename rule. also there's a cleanup step where you mark aliases to the canonical route.
[10:12] [10:30] Leila Wong: how do you handle retained data for debugging — logs vs actual prompts/responses? we need to ensure PII is redacted.
[10:40] Carlos Rivera: by default we don't store full prompts past N days unless you opt-in. we offer PII redaction and token-level hashing; for Private deployments you control the retention policy entirely.
[10:52] [11:10] Samir Desai: what's the quickest way to validate numbers — do you have a sandbox with synthetic traffic we can run?
[11:18] Carlos Rivera: yes we have a sandbox org. for speed we recommend you upload a 24–72 hour replay of sampled requests and we'll run the Optimize estimator against it.
[11:30] Maya Patel: action items recap — i'll send security docs and pricing; carlos will run the perf notes and pilot plan; jordan will drop the CSV.
[11:42] Leila Wong: timeline — we want pilot in two weeks ideally.
[11:46] Maya Patel: we'll aim for POC kickoff week of 2026-10-12.
[11:52] [12:00] Carlos Rivera: any final questions?
[12:03] Leila Wong: none from me, thanks for the walkthrough.
[12:06] Samir Desai: quick note — please include the quantized model performance numbers for T4 vs A100 in the perf doc.
[12:12] Carlos Rivera: will do.
[12:15] Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up by email with attachments.
[12:20] [SCREEN SHARE END]

Transcript notes: occasional speaker mislabels by the recorder (e.g., "Samir" sometimes appears as "Speaker 3"). Some words transcribed imperfectly ("quantization" as "quanti zation"), filler words kept.
